evaluated.name: MarginUpCapexDown

critic_notes.rationale: (oibdp − capx)/at is simply free-cash-flow-to-assets, a long-published profitability/investment measure that is mechanically close to a linear RMW-minus-CMA combination, so it is a rediscovery rather than a genuine cross-theme interaction.

The conditional construction is internally consistent and the sign is right, but the asset-growth-within-profitable-firms effect is close to the q-factor/investment-profitability interaction already in the literature, and the hard-coded 0.12 profitability cutoff is arbitrary and non-stationary across time and industries.

Economically coherent and sign-consistent, but it is an additive difference of two separately documented signals (profitability trend and abnormal capital investment) labelled as a "composite," and the 5-year TREND windows will materially cut coverage without adding a true interaction.

Sign and construction are consistent and the profitability conditioning is a legitimate twist, but the base effect is the well-known acquirer-underperformance/investment anomaly, and COALESCE(aqc,0) creates a large tied mass at zero that will make the rank and hence the long leg mechanically lumpy.

The core driver is the composite external-financing anomaly (Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan) and net share issuance, both heavily published; the cash-flow indicator is a sample split rather than a new mechanism, and mixing a flow (sstk) with a first-difference (DELTA(dltt,1)) is an inconsistent construction.

Within-firm time-series ranking of the profitability-versus-capex-intensity state is a genuinely less-explored construction that purges the stable industry effects contaminating level-based composites, though the coarse 5-period TS_RANK will produce heavy ties and unstable portfolio membership that should be diagnosed.

This is a cosmetic tie-breaking variant of the archive's SelfHistoryProfitCapexWedge — the added leg is just a cross-sectional profitability-minus-investment-intensity spread (essentially RMW/CMA in rank form) — so any improvement measures smoothing of rank ties rather than a new economic mechanism, and the design explicitly admits as much.

The proposal is internally incoherent — EXPECTED_SIGN is declared negative while the reasoning states the operative claim is a positive slope — and beneath the sign confusion it is a near-duplicate of SelfHistoryProfitCapexWedge with oancf swapped for oibdp and aqc folded into capex.

This is a plain rank-difference of two long-published anomalies — profitability (RMW/gross profitability) and net debt issuance (Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan, Spiess-Affleck-Graves) — with no genuine conditioning structure, so it is a rediscovery-plus-linear-combination rather than a cross-theme interaction.

The multiplicative gate is internally consistent with the hypothesis (unprofitable firms shrink toward neutral, extremes populated by profitable non-expanders vs. profitable expanders) and is a defensible continuous replacement for an arbitrary threshold, though the underlying profitability×investment interaction is close to well-trodden RMW/CMA territory and the construction discards the profitability main effect.

Recasting labor productivity as a one-year change rather than an industry-ranked level is a substantive, well-diagnosed response to the earlier signal's negative FF5 alpha, but the second leg (gross plant growth) is simply the asset-growth anomaly and emp-based coverage will remain thin, so the incremental content rests entirely on the productivity-change leg.

Investment second moments are genuinely absent from the archive and the profitability gate is consistently constructed, though the test should control for the likely correlation of capex volatility with size and idiosyncratic volatility, and a 5-period VOL window is a noisy estimator.

This is the archive's SelfHistoryProfitCapexWedge with the capex denominator swapped from ppent to dp — two highly correlated scalings of the same capex-intensity variable — so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the "neutral point at capx/dp=1" argument is void because TS_RANK discards the level entirely.

Internally consistent and it does move the discipline leg from fixed capital to working capital (a genuinely different channel from the capex wedges), but own-history inventory-to-sales is close to the published inventory-growth anomaly and the construction still reuses the archive's wedge template, so the incremental content is modest.

This is essentially the sum of two well-known published anomalies — cash-based operating profitability (Ball et al.) and (ex-cash) asset growth / net-operating-asset growth (Cooper-Gulen-Schill, Hirshleifer et al.) — and stripping cash from at is a documented refinement, so it is unlikely to carry information beyond RMW/CMA rather than repairing the CMA-overlap problem it claims to fix.

The marginal-productivity-of-capex mechanism is genuinely absent from the archive and the hypothesis matches the expression's direction, but scaling by capex means cross-sectional dispersion is dominated by the denominator, so low-capex firms will populate both tails and the signal risks degenerating into an earnings-change-times-inverse-capex-intensity composite that winsorizing at 1% will not fully discipline.

Persistence of sub-maintenance capex is a genuinely new state variable for this archive, the indicator/TS_SUM construction correctly implements the stated hypothesis with the right sign, and the additive SUMRANK form sensibly preserves the profitability main effect that the multiplicative gates destroyed — though the five-level count is coarse and the signal must be shown to beat a plain low-investment-plus-profitability composite.

oancf/oibdp is algebraically one minus accruals-scaled-by-earnings, so the first leg is a restatement of the accrual anomaly rather than a novel profitability-quality dimension, and the ratio is sign-unstable whenever oibdp is small or negative — a defect winsorizing cannot repair, since negative-earnings firms with positive cash flow are ranked as the worst converters.

This is a mechanical SUMRANK ensemble of two already-archived signals rather than a new economic mechanism, and it will teach little beyond what a correlation of the two existing return series would show — especially since one leg (realized return on recent capex) has an essentially zero cross-sectional slope, so any alpha gain is portfolio-averaging, not new information.

Matching the profit-change horizon to a three-year cumulative capex denominator is a substantive, well-motivated repair of the parent ratio's small-denominator noise problem rather than a cosmetic reparameterization, though the tails will still be populated disproportionately by low-capex firms and winsorization alone may not fully fix that.

The mechanism is sensible and distinct from the archive, but the expression is internally flawed because Compustat `intan` already includes `gdwl`, so ADD(intan, gdwl) double-weights goodwill; additionally the acquired-intangible share is a slow-moving, near-monotone series whose five-year TS_RANK will be pinned near 1.0 for most acquirers, giving the second leg little cross-sectional variation.

Scaling capex by cash on hand is a genuinely different funding-constraint denominator that CMA/asset-growth do not span, and TS_RANK tames the near-zero-denominator explosion, but the second leg is close to an inverse own-history cash-level rank, so the sort risks becoming a cash-holdings-plus-profitability signal (a known premium) rather than the investment-discipline story claimed.

This is a near-duplicate of the archived ProfitUpCapexDecelerating — identical profitability-change gate, with only the second leg swapped from capex acceleration to a five-year capex-intensity rank — and it inherits the same multiplicative-gate pathology in which firms with low profit-improvement rank collapse toward zero regardless of investment state, muddying the intended long and short legs.

SG&A intensity is a genuinely untested profitability dimension in this archive that is not what RMW is built on, and the own-history construction is internally consistent with the hypothesis; the main risk is that both legs measure restraint with no profitability level, so the long leg may simply load on shrinking, low-growth firms rather than cash generators.

Economically coherent and internally consistent, but it is the third permutation of the same TS_RANK(profitability) − TS_RANK(capx/ppent) template already tested twice in the archive (oibdp/at at 3.74 and sale/ppent at 4.19), so it is very likely to be a highly correlated rediscovery rather than new information about the mechanism.

The absolute sub-maintenance threshold (capx < dp) is a genuinely different economic condition from the archive's relative-decline indicator, so this is a substantive recombination rather than a cosmetic one, though the capx/dp leg previously delivered essentially zero portfolio alpha and DELTA(capx/dp) is an outlier-prone tie-break term whose scale may swamp the profitability delta unless SUMRANK ranks each argument internally.

This is a one-operator edit of the archive's SelfHistoryProfitCapexWedge and largely duplicates the question already answered by IndustryRelativeDeploymentMismatch (industry-adjusted deployment, fmb 3.45), so the diagnostic value is small relative to its near-certain high correlation with two existing entries.

The expression matches the hypothesis and the negative sign is correct, and since the two joint-event cells are not logical complements the decomposition genuinely tests long/short asymmetry in the archive's best signal, though the coarse 0–5 count with heavy mass at zero will produce unstable portfolio breakpoints on the short leg.

Conditioning on discrete gross-PPE contraction events rather than a spending rate is a materially new investment measurement and pairs it with a profitability variable the archive has barely used, with the main risks being that outright capacity shrinkage overlaps the well-known asset-growth/CMA effect and that rare events plus a five-level count leave heavy ties.

Broadening the investment leg to fixed plus working capital is a real economic redefinition rather than a re-denomination, the accrual-free profitability leg is a sensible control, and the only caution is that oancf-minus-total-investment is close in spirit to a free-cash-flow/net-operating-asset construct, so a known-anomaly overlap check is warranted.

This is an operator-only re-run of the archive's best signal (SelfHistoryProfitCapexWedge) on identical inputs, and the change is asymmetric in a way that likely hurts rather than helps — the long tail of MIN is nearly the same firms as the top of SUB, while the bottom tail now pools two economically opposite failures (low profitability vs. high capex), so the short leg becomes an uninterpretable mixture and the L-S spread is not a clean test of the "joint state" hypothesis.

The diagnosis of why peak-distance failed on the slow-moving net PPE stock is honest and applying it to the capex flow is a legitimate magnitude-preserving alternative to TS_RANK, but capx/TS_MAX(capx,5) will pile a large mass exactly at 1.0 for any firm currently at its own spending peak (common under nominal growth), so the same clustering pathology may reappear in weaker form and the second leg remains highly correlated with the archive's TS_RANK capex term.

The second leg is essentially the published asset/PPE-growth anomaly and the first is a change-in-gross-profitability variable, and the identical construction (RANK of a one-year profitability change minus RANK of GROWTH(ppegt)) was already tested as ProductivityGainWithoutCapacityAdd and ContinuousProfitGatedCapacityGrowth, both of which delivered sign-wrong negative FF5 alphas — swapping the profitability numerator is a cosmetic change to a structure the archive has already rejected.

The diagnosis that dividing by cumulative capex let small-denominator firms populate both tails is specific and correct, and separately ranking a three-year profitability gain against a three-year capex intensity scaled by beginning-of-period plant is a substantively different estimator of the same marginal-return mechanism rather than a relabeling, though the investment leg's overlap with the long-horizon investment/CMA factor should be checked in the FF5 alpha.

Folding a profitability level into the overhead-efficiency leg is a genuine response to OverheadLeanNonDeployer's "both legs measure shrinkage" weakness, but taking TS_RANK of a cross-sectional SUMRANK muddles the interpretation (it now measures whether the firm's peer-relative efficiency is at a five-year high, not whether its efficiency is), and the second leg is byte-identical to the earlier signal, so a strong result will be hard to attribute to the new channel.

The three-year step-down in capex intensity is a genuinely untested timing functional in this archive — distinct from levels, one-year deltas, trends, and own-history ranks — and pairing it with current profitability gives a coherent "post-build-out harvester" long leg, though the combination of profitability level plus falling investment sits close to a simple RMW×CMA repackaging and should be judged on whether the alpha survives FF5.

This is essentially the arithmetic blend of two already-archived signals (SelfHistoryProfitCapexWedge, fmb 3.74, and UtilizationHarvestWedge, fmb 4.19) sharing an identical capx/ppent leg, so it is a combinatorial recombination rather than a new economic channel and will almost certainly land between its two parents.

Switching the joint indicator from year-over-year changes to deviations from a firm's own three-year norm genuinely converts a flip-count into a state-occupancy/duration measure, which is a defensible economic distinction from DivergenceEpisodeCount, though the overlap with that archived signal is large enough that the incremental information may be modest and highly correlated.

The archive already contains this mechanism in both ratio form (ThreeYearMarginalReturnOnCapital) and rank-wedge form, and re-denominating the numerator to ΔROA and the denominator to capex-intensity is a scaling variant, not a new mechanism — and the near-zero-denominator explosion for low-capex firms (exactly the population the hypothesis wants to go long) is only partly contained by 1% winsorization.

The balance-sheet-composition leg is genuinely the first non-flow investment measure in this archive and the trend-vs-trend architecture is validated, but note the mechanical hazard that a falling ppent/at share is largely driven by growth in non-PP&E assets — which the asset-growth anomaly says predicts *low* returns — so the second leg may fight the hypothesized sign.

A legitimate channel swap on the best-performing episode-count architecture, but the stated advantage is backwards — the shared ppent denominator induces mechanical coupling (a shrinking plant raises both legs), so the joint condition largely reduces to sales growth exceeding capex growth rather than a clean output-versus-investment divergence.

The two raw deviations are in incommensurable units and dispersions (ROA deviations of a few percentage points versus capx/ppent deviations an order of magnitude larger), so the un-normalized subtraction will be dominated almost entirely by the capex leg and the signal is not the balanced wedge the hypothesis describes.

The diagnosis is technically correct — because SUMRANK ranks the raw wedge, the capex leg's larger dispersion does dominate the tie-break, so z-scoring is a real repair rather than a monotone relabeling — but this is nonetheless a recombination of the archive's two best entries whose outcome will likely land between them, and the supporting claim that the standardized wedge had "the highest Sharpe in the archive" is false (0.475 vs 0.482).

The argument that net investment (capx−dp) can be negative and therefore loses information under TS_RANK is a genuine measurement point that justifies the z-score form, though the stated premise is wrong — standardization did *not* improve the plain capex wedge (alpha 0.039→0.038, t 4.52→4.32, Sharpe 0.482→0.475) — and VOL of a near-zero net-investment ratio risks unstable denominators despite the winsorization.

Transplanting the duration-plus-intensity architecture to the working-capital channel is a substantive channel test rather than a re-denomination, the two legs are correctly free of a shared denominator, and the prior working-capital evidence is signed consistently in both directions; the main risks are inventory-driven coverage attrition in service industries and partial overlap with the known inventory-growth anomaly.

"High profitability plus falling leverage" is very close to two of the nine Piotroski F-score components (ROA and ΔLEVER) and adjacent to the debt-issuance/net-external-financing anomaly; the within-firm standardization is a real distinction but not obviously enough of one to escape rediscovery, and the proposal does not address that overlap.

The two legs are not an interaction but two mechanically linked pieces of the same DuPont identity — ROA = margin × turnover, so TREND(oibdp/at) minus TREND(sale/ppent, inverted) largely reduces to a margin-trend signal and reproduces Fairfield–Yohn's margin-versus-turnover decomposition, while the "investment discipline" leg contains no investment flow at all.

This is a cosmetic re-scaling of GrossProfitPerInventoryDollarHarvest whose stated justification is self-refuting — it cites the margin wedge's Sharpe going "from 0.48 to 0.475," which is a deterioration, and the same holds for its alpha and t-stat — so the premise that standardization is an upgrade is not supported by the archive it cites.

This is a single-window parameter tweak (MA3→MA5) on the archive's leading HarvestStatePersistenceCount, and the five-year-norm deviation form has already been probed via StandardizedOwnHistoryHarvestWedge, making it a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism.

Requiring simultaneous capex restraint and acquisition abstinence is a genuinely tighter policy definition than either archive parent (closing the capex-vs-M&A substitution loophole) and the indicator directions are internally consistent, though the triple-condition count risks mass concentration at zero and the incremental information over the two existing occupancy signals may be small.

Placing the archive's strongest cross-sectional investment measure (net-of-depreciation investment) inside the occupancy/duration architecture is a coherent and non-redundant combination with correctly signed indicators, and the own-norm framing sensibly avoids the absolute capx<dp threshold that failed twice, though it remains an incremental recombination of two already-validated components.

Swapping the capex denominator from net plant to total assets is a one-parameter rescaling of the leading signal with no new economic content, and the stated coverage benefit is speculative since coverage is bound by the five-year history and profitability terms, not the capex denominator.

The count leg is effectively persistent low equity issuance, which is close to a direct rediscovery of the well-documented share-issuance/net-external-financing anomaly, and the profitability gate plus capex tie-break may not be enough to establish that any measured alpha is incremental to that known effect.

As an ablation it has diagnostic value, but it is nearly the un-standardized MA3 twin of the already-evaluated StandardizedOwnHistoryHarvestWedge and SelfHistoryProfitCapexWedge, and subtracting two raw, differently-scaled ratio deviations without standardization means the high-variance capex/ppent leg will mechanically dominate the wedge.

This is the third interchange of the tie-break leg in an already-tested pairing (raw MA3 deviation in HarvestStatePersistenceCount, standardized deviation in OccupancyCountStandardizedTieBreak, now the TS_RANK wedge already tested standalone as SelfHistoryProfitCapexWedge), so it is a cosmetic recombination of two archived components that will be near-collinear with both and cannot diagnose anything new.

Adding an absolute profitability floor is yet another indicator multiplied into the same occupancy count (structurally identical to DualRestraint/DryPowder), but the specific economic claim — that own-norm profitability admits distressed rebounders whose low capex is constraint rather than choice — is untested and falsifiable, with the acknowledged risk that a level gate pulls the long leg toward RMW.

This is a genuinely new aggregator rather than a re-shuffling of archived legs — MIN of dimensionless proportional deviations enforces conjunction while preserving intensity and cannot be spoofed by the doubly-bad cell — though the unwinsorized capex/ppent-to-own-mean ratio leaves a real outlier tail on the short side that should be checked.

The asymmetric-reference hypothesis (competitive advantage is relative, capital-allocation policy is firm-specific) is coherent and directly completes the question PeerRestraintOccupancy left open, but it is a single-indicator swap in a heavily reused template and the industry-relative profitability level is the leg most likely to be absorbed by FF5's RMW.

Substituting operating cash flow for accrual EBITDA inside the occupancy architecture is a defensible and previously untested measurement choice with a clear economic rationale (harvestable surplus cannot be manufactured by accruals), though it is a one-input swap and the ~0.08–0.11 coverage typical of oancf entries risks an apparent improvement driven by sample selection.

Both legs are already in the archive (NetInvestmentBelowNormOccupancy for the count, NetDisinvestmentHarvestWedge for the TS_RANK wedge) so this is a cosmetic bolt-together, and the stated motivation misdescribes the prior signal's tie-break as volatility-scaled when it in fact used a raw MA3 deviation, undermining the claimed diagnosis.

validation_diagnostics.message: proposal expression does not use any variable exclusive to required theme: investment (variables shared across the paired themes, e.g. common denominators like 'at', do not count as evidence for either theme)
